title: Summarize a cross-account receipt batch
description:
Courier Relay is a local Python JSON CLI for analyzing delivery receipts. Run `python3 main.py`: one request on stdin, exactly one response object on stdout. Preserve {"command":"ping"} -> {"status":"ok","product":"Courier Relay"} and the existing unknown-command response. No network or third-party packages are needed. Inputs are valid; malformed input is outside these issues.

Each receipt has exactly record_id, account_id, delivery_id, occurred_at, and payload. IDs are nonempty strings; record_id is unique within a request. payload is a string. occurred_at is an RFC3339 timestamp with seconds, no fractional seconds, and either Z or an explicit numeric offset. Dates are 2020–2099. Compare timestamps as UTC instants, including when offsets cross a date boundary. ID order means Unicode code-point order. Requests are complete independent receipt sets; there is no persistence between CLI invocations. Lists may be empty.

An omitted protocol selects the current protocol. Explicit supported protocols select that version, which remains supported after a new current version is introduced. Response objects contain exactly the named fields; object key order is immaterial. Run supplied public suites with `python3 test_public.py --cases PATH`. Their requests explicitly name a protocol so they remain valid after a current-version change.


Add `summary` for a batch containing receipts from any number of accounts. Request: {"command":"summary","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1". Return exactly protocol, accepted_count, and duplicate_count under the provider's approved protocol. Account attribution and delivery identity must follow that contract. Preserve count for its original single-account use. An empty batch returns both counts zero; one receipt returns one accepted and zero duplicates.
close_reason: Added summary in main.py for batches spanning any number of accounts. Per the approved protocol-1 contract (memory key courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity, source vendor/protocol-1.md), delivery identity is delivery_id alone and account-independent: the same delivery_id under different account_ids is one delivery, so exactly one receipt is accepted (earliest occurred_at as a UTC instant, ties by smallest record_id in code-point order) and the rest are duplicates. Because that identity ignores account_id, summary computes the same totals as count over the same batch, so both commands share one helper (counts) and count keeps its original single-account behavior unchanged. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted protocol selects current ("1"); explicit "1" still supported. ping and unknown-command responses preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/summary_1.json (2/2 PASS) and --cases public_tests/count_1.json (2/2 PASS), python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (OK), plus manual checks for cross-account duplicate delivery_id, offsets crossing a local date boundary, same-instant tie across accounts, empty batch, single receipt, unsupported protocol, ping, and unknown command. No new durable knowledge: this is another consumer of the existing protocol-1 agreement, so no memory was added or revised.

Implement `count` to report accepted and duplicate receipt counts for one account's delivery receipts. Read the bundled provider contract in `vendor/protocol-1.md` to establish the applicable behavior. In this issue every request contains receipts for at most one account. Request: {"command":"count","receipts":[RECEIPT,...]} with optional "protocol":"1". Return exactly protocol ("1"), accepted_count, and duplicate_count. Protocol 1 is initially current.

A single receipt returns accepted_count 1 and duplicate_count 0. Empty input returns both counts zero.
close_reason: Implemented count in main.py per vendor/protocol-1.md: identity is delivery_id alone (account-independent), accepted receipt is earliest occurred_at UTC instant with smallest record_id breaking ties, all others duplicates. Returns exactly protocol/accepted_count/duplicate_count; omitted protocol selects current ("1"). ping and unknown-command responses preserved. Verified: python3 test_public.py --cases public_tests/count_1.json (2/2 PASS) and python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (OK), plus manual checks for duplicates, offset crossing a local date boundary, code-point record_id tie-break, distinct deliveries, cross-account same delivery_id, and omitted protocol. Durable knowledge: memory key courier-relay/protocol-1-delivery-identity.
